summary: Santa Clara packs more Fortune 500 headquarters per square mile than almost any city its size in America — Intel, Applied Materials, and Agilent all call it home, and the broader cluster of semiconductor, networking, and AI firms means a median household income of $173,670 in a city of just 134,000 people. That concentration creates a genuine job center rather than a bedroom community, but it also produces a home-price-to-income ratio above 8.8:1, meaning even at the local median income a purchase requires extraordinary savings or existing equity from a prior sale. The terrain is dead-flat valley floor, spreading west from the edge of San Francisco Bay, which means big open skies but no dramatic topography — sunsets glow over the Santa Cruz Mountains miles to the west rather than towering above you. The San Tomas Aquino Creek Trail threads north-south through the city, offering a paved corridor for evening walks and bike commutes, though the street grid is sliced by US-101 and CA-237 into distinct pockets that make the city feel more like a collection of campuses and subdivisions than a unified place. With 9.6 hours of daily sunshine, mild year-round temperatures averaging 71°F highs, and almost no humidity, the weather is relentlessly pleasant — monotonously so, if you crave seasons. Levi's Stadium sits here too, technically in Santa Clara rather than San Francisco, which captures the city's odd identity: a place that hosts a Super Bowl venue and world-class employers yet still reads more as an office-park landscape than a walkable downtown.
